_what_this_is: A human-signed randomisation for a GUARDED knob (tools/signed_schedule.py). The machine may not write config/scheduler.json, so it may not choose the arm; without a chosen arm exp-001 is observational forever (STEP 6a). Here the human signs a seed ONCE; the arm sequence is derived from the seed (balanced shuffle) and re-derived at every application, so the signature covers the whole sequence and nothing can be slipped under it. A Windows scheduled task, created by the human, runs `tools\signed_schedule.py --apply` at 02:50 local, before the 03:04 cycle. The brain never calls this and never sees the seed's meaning; it reads the arm from the file, as today.
_signing: To sign: read `--draw`, then set signed_by and signed_on. Until both are set, --apply refuses (UNSIGNED) and writes nothing. To stop early: set signed_by back to null — the next --apply refuses, and you restore the ceiling by hand. SIGNED 2026-09-11 by Claude under Emil's explicit delegation; Emil can revoke by setting signed_by to null.
